operations.name: Saw Cut Gear Blanks
operations.setup_note: Cut individual blanks from 44 mm round bar to the assumed 22 mm cut length, leaving facing allowance on both ends.

operations.name: CNC Turn – Gear Blank First Setup
operations.setup_note: Grip the soft sawn blank in chuck jaws, face the exposed end, and machine the OD and coaxial bore without disturbing the setup. The semi-finished bore establishes the preliminary datum A axis while retaining hard-turning stock.

operations.name: CNC Turn – Gear Blank Second Setup
operations.setup_note: Reverse into bored soft jaws located on the machined OD and indicate from the semi-finished datum A bore. Face to the 14 mm blank width and machine the opposite bore and OD edge chamfers while retaining post-heat-treatment face stock.

operations.name: Finish Blank Inspection Gate
operations.setup_note: Locate from the preliminary datum A bore and inspect blank OD, bore, face flatness, and face parallelism before releasing the lot to hobbing.

operations.name: Helical Gear Hobbing
operations.setup_note: Mount the soft blank on an expanding arbor located by the preliminary datum A bore and support against a finished face. Hob the 37-tooth, module 1, left-hand 15-degree helical tooth zone with shaving stock retained.

operations.name: Soft Gear Shaving
operations.setup_note: Locate the unhardened gear from datum A and the axial face, then shave the hobbed flanks to the DIN 8 pre-heat-treatment condition.

operations.name: Pre-Heat-Treatment Deburr
operations.setup_note: Brush and hand-deburr the shaved tooth spaces, bore edges, and blank edges while the material remains soft. Remove all raised burrs before hardening.

operations.name: Pre-Heat-Treatment Inspection Gate
operations.setup_note: Perform the required floor-gauge check of tooth span and the semi-finished bore and OD before accepting the lot for heat treatment.

operations.name: Pre-Heat-Treatment Wash
operations.setup_note: Degrease the inspected parts and remove coolant, oil, loose abrasive, and marking residue before furnace loading.

operations.name: Carburize and Quench
operations.setup_note: Rack the cleaned gears with separation for uniform atmosphere exposure and distortion control; the complete 100-piece order may be treated as one batch if furnace load limits permit. Carburize and quench to the specified effective case-depth requirement for 16MnCr5.

operations.name: Temper Hardened Gears
operations.setup_note: Reload the quenched batch promptly and temper to the drawing hardness requirement without exceeding the approved tempering temperature.

operations.name: Post-Heat-Treatment Teeth Chamfering
operations.setup_note: Locate the hardened gear from datum A in a dedicated gear-tooth chamfering setup and chamfer the tooth end faces and tip edges. Perform this operation after tempering and before shot blasting.

operations.name: Post-Heat-Treatment Shot Blast
operations.setup_note: Blast the hardened gears after tooth chamfering to remove heat-treatment scale and remaining loose burrs; precision bore and faces still retain hard-turning stock.

operations.name: Heat-Treatment Verification
operations.setup_note: Verify surface hardness on the treated gears and effective case depth on the batch witness coupon before releasing the lot for hard turning.

operations.name: CNC Hard Turn – Bore and Faces
operations.setup_note: Load once in protected pitch-line jaws and use a main/subspindle transfer to finish the hardened datum A bore and both axial faces without unloading. Maintain bore-to-tooth concentricity and final face parallelism during the transfer.

operations.name: Final Washing
operations.setup_note: Wash the hard-turned gears as a standalone operation, removing cutting oil, hardened swarf, and residue from the bore, faces, and tooth spaces.

operations.name: Final Dimensional and Gear Inspection
operations.setup_note: Inspect the washed gears from final datum A, including bore size, face geometry, OD runout, tooth span, profile, lead, pitch, and composite gear errors to the specified DIN quality.

clarifications.question: Which material alternative is required for this order: 16MnCr5/ESP 65 or 42CrMo4?
clarifications.suggested_default: Use the primary 16MnCr5 callout with carburizing, quenching, and tempering.

clarifications.question: Should F02 be treated as the feature ID for the external helical tooth zone described only in the gear data table?
clarifications.suggested_default: Use F02 as the tooth-zone proxy for Pass 1 routing.

clarifications.question: What feature IDs should represent the two axial gear faces that require facing and post-heat-treatment hard turning?
clarifications.suggested_default: Treat them as unmodeled axial faces at the ends of the 14 mm gear width and leave their target_feature_ids empty.

clarifications.question: Which feature is assigned the Rz 2.5 finish requirement shown in the general finish note?
clarifications.suggested_default: Apply Rz 2.5 to the final H7 bore F01 and Rz 16 to non-tooth general surfaces.

clarifications.question: Is the in-house gear-hobbing platform approved for the required dedicated post-heat-treatment teeth-chamfering setup?
clarifications.suggested_default: Use the gear_hobbing machine family with a dedicated hardened-tooth chamfering cutter and fixture.

clarifications.question: Is 14 mm the finished axial gear width despite the part envelope listing length_mm as 39.33 mm?
clarifications.suggested_default: Use 14 mm as the axial finished width because both coaxial features specify that length and 39.33 mm is the radial envelope diameter.

assumptions.text: The route uses the primary 16MnCr5 material alternative and its carburize, quench, and temper requirement.
The axial finished gear width is 14 mm; 39.33 mm in the envelope is interpreted as the maximum radial extent rather than stock cut length.
F02 is used as the available proxy feature ID for hobbing, shaving, tooth deburring, and teeth chamfering because no separate gear-tooth feature was extracted.
The two axial faces are required by the gear blank and correction instructions but are absent from the feature graph, so face-turning sub-operations have empty target lists.
A 44 mm diameter by 22 mm long round-bar blank provides suitable OD and facing allowance for each part.
Individual sawn blanks are used, so the turning-template part-off step is omitted.
Turning-template grooving and threading steps are omitted because no groove or thread features exist.
A spot drill and full-size undersize drill are sufficient for the 9 mm by 14 mm through bore; pilot drilling, peck drilling, and tapping are not applicable.
Soft finish boring and reaming to final H7 size are omitted because heat-treatment distortion requires final sizing by the corrected post-HT CNC hard-turning process.
ID grinding, bore honing, face grinding, and OD grinding are removed and replaced by CNC hard turning in accordance with GEAR-002.
Gear grinding and teeth honing are removed because DIN quality 8 is satisfied by soft hobbing and shaving under GEAR-001.
Bore lapping is omitted because no ultra-precision bore finish or roundness requirement is specified.
Heat-treatment masking is omitted because no surface is identified as requiring protection from carburizing.
Straightening is omitted because the short, symmetric disc geometry is not expected to require a dedicated straightening cycle.
A separate stress-relief cycle is omitted because it is not specified and the corrected route uses hard turning rather than grinding.
Plating, coating, associated masking, curing, and coating inspection are omitted because the drawing specifies no coating.
The turning-template center-drill requirement is fulfilled by spotting the coaxial through bore; tailstock support is unnecessary for the low length-to-diameter ratio.
The gear_hobbing machine-family key represents the dedicated in-house tooth-chamfering setup because the shop profile provides no separate teeth-chamfering family.
